recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work should address specific new BR&R trackers against AdministrableProductDefinition or the Medication Definition module, not reopen FHIR-14718 as a generic request for better pre-ballot documentation.
issue_request: FHIR-14718 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R change request against the STU3 MedicinalProductPharmaceutical ballot page. It said the resource had insufficient Description of Resource and Scope and Usage documentation and asked for improvement before formal ballot, especially to explain how it relates to other medication resources. The final Jira comments record agreement with the concern and planned substantial improvements for R5.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-14718. The old MedicinalProductPharmaceutical source was replaced during R5 medication-definition work: commit 143e1ea5 added AdministrableProductDefinition as the successor resource, and commit 0d8e328 substantially rewrote its Scope and Usage narrative and linked it to the Medication Definition module. Current fhir.ini keeps an R4/R5 conversion mapping from MedicinalProductPharmaceutical to AdministrableProductDefinition.
additional_context: Later BR&R decisions reinforce the current shape rather than requiring another edit. FHIR-28581 asked to collapse MedicinalProductDefinition, MedicinalProductPharmaceutical/AdministrableProductDefinition, and PackagedProductDefinition; its Published resolution says the resource definitions were considerably enhanced to explain why the boundaries were selected. FHIR-39252 asked for ISO IDMP naming clarification, and the current AdministrableProductDefinition Scope and Usage text includes that clarification and links to the Medication Definition and Medications modules.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. AdministrableProductDefinition is active in the current build, the retired MedicinalProductPharmaceutical source folder is no longer present, fhir.ini maps the retired name to AdministrableProductDefinition, and the current narrative/definition now explains scope, use, relationship to manufactured items, relationship to Medication for administered instances, and the IDMP Pharmaceutical Product naming relationship.

related_jiras.note: Later Published ballot issue challenged the same product-resource boundaries, and its resolution confirms those definitions had been considerably enhanced rather than collapsed.
Later Published ballot issue clarified why FHIR uses AdministrableProductDefinition for the ISO IDMP Pharmaceutical Product concept; the current Scope and Usage includes that clarification.
